title: Displacement of families from Pakistan-occupied areas
place_name: Mirpur, Muzaffarabad, Bhimber, Kotli and other occupied areas
summary: The 1947 war displaced 31,619 families from areas that came under Pakistani occupation, according to the Union government. Of these, 26,319 families registered and settled in Jammu and Kashmir, and 5,300 moved to other parts of India. Many still await full rehabilitation.

title: Invasion of Muzaffarabad and killings at Domel
summary: On 22 October 1947 tribal lashkars, armed, transported and led by Pakistan Army officers, crossed into Jammu and Kashmir and took Muzaffarabad within days. Hindu and Sikh residents and refugees were killed, their homes looted and burnt, and many women abducted. Men rounded up near Domel were shot and their bodies thrown into the river. India marks 22 October as a Black Day for the invasion.

title: Sack of Baramulla
place_name: Baramulla, including St Joseph's Convent and hospital
victim_community: Hindu, Sikh, Christian and Muslim residents
summary: The lashkars reached Baramulla on 26 October 1947 and spent days looting the town instead of pressing on to Srinagar. Raiders stormed St Joseph's Convent and its hospital, killing nuns, staff and patients. Survivors estimated that about 3,000 townspeople were killed. The delay gave India time to fly troops into Srinagar.

title: Indian troops airlifted to Srinagar after accession
summary: Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession to India on 26 October 1947. From the morning of 27 October the Indian Army flew its first troops into Srinagar airfield to stop the advance of the invaders on the city. The airlift is regarded as the step that saved Srinagar.

title: Fall of Bhimber
summary: Bhimber fell to Pakistan-backed forces in the early hours of 28 October 1947, the first town in the south of the state to be captured. Accounts describe men being killed and women and children taken hostage. No reliable toll has been found.

title: Killings of prisoners at Alibeg camp
summary: Hindu and Sikh survivors from Mirpur and nearby areas were held in a gurdwara at Alibeg that Pakistani forces turned into a prison camp. Many were killed and others died of disease and hunger. The Red Cross reached the camp in early 1948 and about 1,600 survivors were moved to India in March 1948.

title: Gilgit Scouts revolt and seizure of Gilgit
summary: On 1 November 1947 the Gilgit Scouts revolted, arrested the state's Governor and declared for Pakistan, which took over the area soon after. The revolt cut Gilgit off from the state and opened the way for attacks on Skardu and Ladakh.

title: Rajouri massacre
summary: Pakistani troops and raiders captured Rajouri on 7 November 1947, when the town was crowded with Hindu and Sikh refugees from the west. Killings peaked around Diwali on 11 and 12 November, and many women took their own lives to avoid capture. The town remained under occupation until the Indian Army retook it on 12 to 13 April 1948.

title: Battle of Shalateng
summary: Indian troops routed the main body of the invaders at Shalateng on the edge of Srinagar on 7 November 1947. The victory ended the threat to the city and opened the way to retake Baramulla and Uri.

title: Siege of Poonch
summary: Poonch, crowded with refugees, was surrounded by Pakistani forces from late November 1947. Under Brigadier Pritam Singh the garrison and residents built an airstrip in about a week, and supplies came in by air from December 1947 despite shelling. The siege was broken in November 1948 when a relief force linked up with the garrison.

title: Mirpur massacre
summary: Mirpur, home to some 25,000 to 30,000 Hindus and Sikhs including refugees, fell to Pakistani forces and raiders on 25 November 1947 after a night of shelling. Thousands were killed within a day and many women took their own lives. About 3,500 survivors were held at a camp at Alibeg, while others reached Jammu on foot.

title: Battle of Naushera
summary: In February 1948 the 50 Parachute Brigade under Brigadier Mohammad Usman beat back a major Pakistani assault on Naushera. The brigade later retook Jhangar.

title: Indian Army retakes Rajouri
summary: Indian troops recaptured Rajouri on 12 to 13 April 1948 after five months of occupation. They found the town ruined and its Hindu and Sikh population largely killed or gone.

title: Brigadier Mohammad Usman killed at Jhangar
summary: Brigadier Mohammad Usman, who had held Naushera and retaken Jhangar, was killed by a Pakistani shell on 3 July 1948. He remains the highest-ranking Indian officer killed in battle, and the Army marks Jhangar Day in his memory.

title: Fall of Skardu and killing of the garrison
victim_community: Hindu and Sikh refugees and soldiers
summary: The 6th Jammu and Kashmir Infantry under Lt Col Sher Jung Thapa held Skardu fort for about six months against forces from Gilgit. Out of food and ammunition, the garrison surrendered on 14 August 1948. Soldiers and the refugees sheltering with them were then killed, and women in the garrison took their own lives. Thapa was taken prisoner.

title: Operation Bison, tanks at Zoji La
summary: On 1 November 1948 Indian light tanks crossed Zoji La at more than 11,500 feet and surprised the Pakistani-backed forces holding the pass. The attack reopened the road to Kargil and Ladakh.

title: Ceasefire ends the first war
summary: A UN-brokered ceasefire took effect at midnight on 1 January 1949. Pakistan was left in occupation of Mirpur, Muzaffarabad, parts of Poonch and the Gilgit region. The ceasefire line was fixed by the Karachi Agreement of July 1949.

title: Operation Gibraltar, Pakistani infiltration into Kashmir
place_name: Ceasefire line from Kargil to Mendhar
summary: From the night of 5 August 1965 Pakistan sent armed infiltrators, many of them soldiers dressed as locals, across the ceasefire line through routes in Gurez, Tithwal, Uri, Poonch, Rajouri and Kargil. The plan was to start an uprising in the Valley. Local people did not rise and often reported the infiltrators to the authorities, and the operation failed.

title: Indian paratroopers capture the Haji Pir pass
summary: To cut the main infiltration route into the Valley, 1 Para under Major Ranjit Singh Dyal climbed about 4,000 feet overnight and took the Haji Pir pass on the morning of 28 August 1965. Dyal received the Maha Vir Chakra. The pass was handed back to Pakistan under the Tashkent Declaration of 1966.

title: Operation Grand Slam, Pakistani armoured attack at Chhamb
summary: At 4 am on 1 September 1965 Pakistan attacked on the Chhamb and Akhnoor axis with an infantry division and Patton tanks, aiming to cut the road linking Jammu to the Valley. Chhamb fell on 2 September and Jaurian on 4 September. The advance was halted short of Akhnoor as India opened new fronts in Punjab.

title: Ceasefire ends the 1965 war
place_name: Jammu and Kashmir and the Punjab front
summary: A UN-backed ceasefire took effect on 23 September 1965. Under the Tashkent Declaration signed on 10 January 1966, both sides pulled back to positions held before 5 August 1965, which meant India returned the Haji Pir pass.

title: Hijacking of Indian Airlines flight Ganga to Lahore
place_name: Srinagar to Jammu flight, taken to Lahore
summary: On 30 January 1971 two members of the National Liberation Front, Hashim Qureshi and his cousin, hijacked the Indian Airlines Fokker Friendship Ganga soon after take-off from Srinagar and forced it to land at Lahore. Passengers and crew were sent back to India, but the aircraft was destroyed on the ground in Lahore. India responded by banning Pakistani flights over its territory, which hampered Pakistan later that year.

title: Turtuk and nearby villages retaken in Ladakh
place_name: Turtuk, Chalunkha, Thang and Takshi, Nubra
summary: In December 1971 troops led by Major Chewang Rinchen of the Ladakh Scouts advanced about 22 km through mountains in winter, without artillery support. They retook more than 800 sq km held by Pakistan since 1948, including the villages of Turtuk, Chalunkha, Thang and Takshi.

title: Battle of Chhamb, 1971
summary: On the night of 3 to 4 December 1971 Pakistan attacked in the Chhamb sector with a strong force, alongside air strikes on Indian airfields that opened the war in the west. India lost Chhamb for the second time in six years.

title: Simla Agreement and the Line of Control
summary: India and Pakistan signed the Simla Agreement on 2 July 1972 after the 1971 war. The ceasefire line at the end of the 1971 war became the Line of Control, and both sides agreed to settle differences bilaterally.

title: Abduction and killing of diplomat Ravindra Mhatre in Birmingham
summary: In February 1984 Indian diplomat Ravindra Mhatre was abducted in Birmingham by militants who demanded the release of JKLF founder Maqbool Bhat, and was then killed. Maqbool Bhat was hanged in Delhi soon after.

title: Operation Meghdoot secures the Siachen glacier
place_name: Bilafond La and Sia La, Saltoro Ridge
summary: On 13 April 1984, Baisakhi day, the Indian Army and Air Force began Operation Meghdoot and took the main passes of the Saltoro Ridge, Bilafond La and Sia La. The move pre-empted a Pakistani plan to occupy the heights, and India has held the Siachen glacier since.

title: Anantnag riots against Kashmiri Pandits
place_name: Wanpoh, Bijbehara, Akura and other villages of Anantnag
summary: From around 20 February 1986 mobs in Anantnag district attacked Kashmiri Pandit homes, shops and temples, starting at Wanpoh and spreading to Bijbehara and other villages. Temples were desecrated and burnt and houses looted. The riots are widely seen as an early warning of the 1990 exodus.

title: Operation Rajiv, capture of Quaid post on Siachen
summary: In June 1987 a party of 8 JAK LI attacked Quaid post, a Pakistani position overlooking Indian posts on Siachen, after two nights of artillery fire on 25 and 26 June. Naib Subedar Bana Singh led the final assault and received the Param Vir Chakra, and the post was renamed Bana Top.

title: Bomb blasts at Srinagar Telegraph Office and Golf Course
place_name: Central Telegraph Office and Golf Course, Srinagar
summary: On 31 July 1988 JKLF militants set off two bombs in Srinagar, one at the Central Telegraph Office and one at the Golf Course. The blasts are usually taken as the start of the armed insurgency in the Valley.

title: Killing of National Conference leader Mohammad Yusuf Halwai
summary: Mohammad Yusuf Halwai, a National Conference leader, was shot dead in daylight in downtown Srinagar on 21 August 1989. He is often described as the first political victim of the militancy in the Valley.

title: Killing of Tika Lal Taploo
summary: Tika Lal Taploo, a High Court advocate and vice-president of the BJP in the state, was shot dead in Srinagar on 14 September 1989. He was the first prominent Kashmiri Pandit leader to be killed, and his death spread fear through the community. The JKLF was blamed but the case stayed unsolved for decades.

title: Killing of retired judge Neelkanth Ganjoo
place_name: Hari Singh High Street, near the High Court, Srinagar
summary: Neelkanth Ganjoo, the judge who had sentenced JKLF founder Maqbool Bhat to death, was shot dead near the High Court in Srinagar on 4 November 1989. Suspicion fell on the JKLF but no one was arrested. The State Investigation Agency reopened the case in 2023.

title: Abduction of Rubaiya Sayeed and release of five militants
summary: Rubaiya Sayeed, daughter of Union Home Minister Mufti Mohammad Sayeed, was abducted in Srinagar on 8 December 1989. She was freed on 13 December after the government released five jailed JKLF militants. The exchange is widely seen as having emboldened armed groups. She later identified JKLF chief Yasin Malik in court as one of her abductors.

title: Killing of advocate Prem Nath Bhat
summary: Advocate Prem Nath Bhat was shot dead by militants at Khah Bazar in Anantnag on 27 December 1989. His killing came days before the mass flight of Kashmiri Pandits from the Valley in January 1990.

title: Exodus of Kashmiri Pandits from the Valley
place_name: Srinagar and towns across the Kashmir Valley
summary: On the night of 19 January 1990 slogans against Kashmiri Pandits were broadcast from mosque loudspeakers and crowds gathered in the streets, after months of targeted killings and threats. Over the following weeks and months almost all Pandit families left the Valley for Jammu, Delhi and elsewhere, many living for years in camps. Official records count 64,827 families who left in the early 1990s.

title: Killing of four IAF personnel at Rawalpora
summary: On 25 January 1990 gunmen in a car opened fire on Indian Air Force personnel waiting for transport at Rawalpora on the outskirts of Srinagar. Squadron Leader Ravi Khanna and three other airmen were killed and dozens injured. The CBI charged JKLF chief Yasin Malik and others, and in 2024 a surviving airman identified Malik in court as the main shooter.

title: Killing of Satish Tickoo
summary: Satish Tickoo, a young Kashmiri Pandit social worker, was shot at his home in Habba Kadal, Srinagar on 2 February 1990 and died in hospital. Former JKLF militant Farooq Ahmad Dar, known as Bitta Karate, is accused of the killing, and his family's plea to reopen the trial was heard in Srinagar courts in 2022.

title: Killing of Doordarshan Srinagar director Lassa Kaul
summary: Lassa Kaul, director of Doordarshan in Srinagar, was shot dead outside his home at Bemina on 13 February 1990. He was one of a series of Kashmiri Pandits in public life killed in the first months of 1990.

title: Abduction and killing of Kashmir University VC Mushir-ul-Haq and HMT manager H.L. Khera
summary: Militants abducted Kashmir University Vice Chancellor Mushir-ul-Haq and his secretary Abdul Gani on 6 April 1990, along with HMT general manager H.L. Khera, to force the release of jailed associates. The hostages were killed on 10 April. The CBI charged members of the Jammu and Kashmir Students Liberation Front, but they were acquitted and the Supreme Court upheld the acquittal.

title: Abduction and killing of nurse Sarla Bhat
summary: Sarla Bhat, a young Kashmiri Pandit nurse at the Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences, was abducted and killed, and her body was left in downtown Srinagar in April 1990. In 2026 the State Investigation Agency filed a chargesheet naming JKLF chief Yasin Malik and four others.

title: Killing of poet Sarvanand Kaul Premi and his son
summary: Armed men took the Kashmiri poet Sarvanand Kaul Premi and his son from their home in Anantnag district on the night of 29 to 30 April 1990. Their bodies were found days later with signs of torture. The State Investigation Agency reopened the case and in 2026 searched properties linked to a slain militant from Rajouri.

title: Assassination of Mirwaiz Maulvi Mohammad Farooq
summary: Mirwaiz Maulvi Mohammad Farooq, the chief cleric of Kashmir, was shot dead at his home in Nigeen, Srinagar on 21 May 1990. Police attributed the killing to Hizbul Mujahideen militants and arrested two accused who had been absconding for 33 years in 2023.

title: Sarthal bus massacre, Kishtwar
summary: On 14 August 1993 militants stopped a bus in the Sarthal area near Kishtwar, let women and children off, separated the Hindu men and shot them. Published accounts put the dead at 16 or 17. It was the first mass killing of Hindus in the Doda belt and was raised in the Lok Sabha two days later.

title: Burning of Charar-e-Sharif shrine and town
summary: Foreign militants led by Pakistani commander Mast Gul occupied the 14th-century shrine of Sheikh Noor-ud-din Noorani at Charar-e-Sharif in early 1995, leading to a standoff of about two months. On the night of 11 May 1995 fire destroyed the wooden shrine and hundreds of homes in the town. Mast Gul escaped to Pakistan.

title: Al-Faran kidnapping of foreign trekkers
summary: In early July 1995 a group calling itself Al-Faran, a front of Harkat-ul-Ansar, abducted Western trekkers near Pahalgam and demanded the release of jailed militants. American John Childs escaped. Norwegian Hans Christian Ostro was killed in August 1995. The other four hostages were never released, and one account says they were shot in December 1995.

title: Barshalla massacre
summary: On 5 January 1996 militants killed 15 or 16 Hindus at Barshalla village in the Doda belt, ten of them from one family. It was the second mass killing of Hindus in the region after the 1993 Kishtwar bus massacre.

title: Sangrampora massacre
summary: On the eve of Nowroz in March 1997, masked gunmen called Kashmiri Pandit men out of their homes in the small hamlet of Sangrampora in Budgam, saying an officer wanted to speak to them, and shot them. Seven or eight were killed. The case registered in 1997 remains unsolved, and both Pandit and Muslim families later left the village.

title: Wandhama massacre
summary: On the night of 25 January 1998, the eve of Republic Day, gunmen in army-style uniforms entered four Kashmiri Pandit homes in Wandhama village and shot 23 people, including women and children. The families had stayed on in the village after the 1990 exodus. The killings drove more Pandits out of the Valley, and the State Investigation Agency reopened the case in 2026.

title: Prankote and Dakikote massacre
summary: On the night of 17 April 1998 a large group of militants, most of them foreign Lashkar-e-Taiba fighters according to police, attacked the hamlets of Prankote and Dakikote in Mahore tehsil and killed 29 Hindu villagers, many of them women and children. Houses were set on fire. Help took many hours to arrive, and surviving families fled the area.

title: Chapnari wedding party massacre
summary: On 19 June 1998 militants stopped two Hindu wedding parties returning home near Chapnari in Doda, lined up the men and shot them in front of the women. About 25 were killed, among them two bridegrooms. Police said seven militants, four of them foreigners, carried out the attack.

title: Thakrai and Sarwan massacre
place_name: Thakrai and Sarwan villages, Kishtwar area
summary: On 28 July 1998 militants shot dead 16 civilians in Thakrai and the neighbouring village of Sarwan. It was one of six massacres that killed 132 Hindus in the Jammu region and Himachal Pradesh in 1998.

title: Chamba massacre of labourers
place_name: Kalaban and Satrundi villages, Chamba district, Himachal Pradesh
summary: Militants who crossed from the Doda area into Himachal Pradesh killed 35 labourers in Kalaban and Satrundi villages of Chamba district early on 3 August 1998. The workers had camped there to carry supplies to the Pangi valley. It was the first major terrorist attack in Himachal Pradesh.

title: Kargil war (Operation Vijay)
place_name: Kargil, Drass, Batalik, Mushkoh and Turtuk sectors
summary: In early 1999 Pakistani troops crossed the Line of Control and occupied heights in the Kargil sector. India detected the intrusion in May and launched Operation Vijay, retaking the peaks in costly assaults through June and July. The operation ended on 26 July 1999, now marked as Kargil Vijay Diwas. India lost 527 soldiers by the official count, with 1,363 wounded.

title: Capture and killing of Captain Saurabh Kalia's patrol
summary: Captain Saurabh Kalia and five soldiers of 4 Jat were captured by the Pakistan Army on 15 May 1999 after their patrol ran out of ammunition in the Kaksar area. They were held for about three weeks and tortured. Pakistan handed over their bodies on 9 June 1999, and Kalia's family has sought international action since.

title: Fidayeen attack on 15 Corps headquarters, Badami Bagh
summary: On 3 November 1999 fidayeen attacked the headquarters of the Army's 15 Corps at Badami Bagh in Srinagar, killing eight soldiers including Major Purushottam. After Kargil, Lashkar-e-Taiba began a campaign of such suicide squad raids on army and police camps.

title: Hijacking of Indian Airlines IC 814 to Kandahar
summary: Indian Airlines flight IC 814 from Kathmandu was hijacked on 24 December 1999 and taken to Kandahar in Taliban-ruled Afghanistan. After a week, India freed three jailed militants, Masood Azhar, Omar Saeed Sheikh and Mushtaq Zargar, in exchange for the passengers. Masood Azhar founded Jaish-e-Mohammed weeks later.

title: Chittisinghpura massacre of Sikhs
summary: On the evening of 20 March 2000, the eve of US President Bill Clinton's visit to India, gunmen in combat dress rounded up Sikh men in Chittisinghpura village and shot them in front of the two gurdwaras. Thirty-four or 35 were killed. The government blamed Lashkar-e-Taiba and Hizbul Mujahideen.

title: First suicide car bombing in Kashmir, Badami Bagh
summary: On 19 April 2000 a car packed with explosives was blown up outside the Army's 15 Corps headquarters at Badami Bagh in Srinagar, the first suicide bombing in Kashmir. It marked the arrival of Jaish-e-Mohammed in the Valley.

title: Massacre at Amarnath base camp, Nunwan, Pahalgam
victim_community: Hindu pilgrims and local Muslim shopkeepers
summary: On the night of 1 to 2 August 2000 militants attacked the Amarnath yatra base camp at Nunwan near Pahalgam and killed 32 people: pilgrims, local Muslim shopkeepers and security personnel. It was one of five coordinated massacres over those days that killed at least 89 people across Anantnag, Doda and Kupwara.

title: Killing of migrant labourers at Mir Bazar, Qazigund and Achabal
summary: In simultaneous attacks on the same night as the Pahalgam massacre, militants killed 27 migrant labourers at Mir Bazar near Qazigund and at Sandoo near Achabal in Anantnag district. The victims were workers from outside the state.

title: Killings in Doda villages, August 2000
summary: As part of the same wave, militants killed 11 people in a remote village in Doda and ambushed a Village Defence Committee patrol at Kayar, killing at least eight. Both attacks fell within the first days of August 2000.

title: Killing of a surrendered militant's family in Kupwara
summary: In the fourth of the August 2000 attacks, militants killed seven members of the family of a surrendered militant in a village in Kupwara district. The attack targeted the relatives of a man who had left militancy.

title: Kot Charwal massacre of Gujjar families
victim_community: Gujjar Muslim families of Village Defence Committee members
summary: On the night of 9 to 10 February 2001 militants locked 15 members of three Gujjar Muslim families, whose men served in the Village Defence Committee, inside their homes in a remote hamlet of Kot Charwal in Rajouri and set the houses on fire. Seven children and three women were among the dead.

title: Attack on Amarnath pilgrims at Sheshnag
summary: Before dawn on 20 July 2001 militants got past the security cordon at the Sheshnag camp on the Amarnath route, set off explosives and fired on pilgrims. Thirteen people were killed: eight pilgrims, three local Muslim civilians and two security personnel.

title: Loodar massacre near Kishtwar
summary: On 3 August 2001 militants killed Hindu villagers at Loodar near Kishtwar. Fifteen bodies were cremated at Atholi, and later counts put the dead at 17. A Lashkar-e-Taiba militant accused in the killings was shot dead by security forces three days later.

title: Car bomb and fidayeen attack on the J&K Legislative Assembly
summary: On 1 October 2001 a car bomb exploded at the gate of the old Legislative Assembly complex in Srinagar and fidayeen tried to storm the building. At least 38 people were killed, many of them civilians, and the three attackers died. Jaish-e-Mohammed was behind the attack.

title: Attack on the Parliament of India
summary: On 13 December 2001 five armed men from Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed attacked the Parliament complex in New Delhi. Eight security personnel and a gardener were killed and all five attackers died. The attack led to a massive Indian military mobilisation on the border with Pakistan.

title: Fidayeen attack on Raghunath temple, Jammu
summary: On 30 March 2002 fidayeen stormed the Raghunath temple complex in the heart of Jammu city. Eleven devotees were killed and more than 20 injured before the attackers were killed.

title: Kaluchak massacre
place_name: Bus near Kaluchak and Army family quarters, Kaluchak cantonment, Jammu
summary: Early on 14 May 2002 militants in army fatigues stopped a passenger bus near Kaluchak outside Jammu and shot passengers, then entered the family quarters of the Army cantonment and killed mostly women and children of soldiers' families. More than 30 were killed and over 60 wounded. The attack came during a visit by a senior US official.

title: Assassination of Abdul Ghani Lone
summary: Abdul Ghani Lone, a senior moderate leader of the Hurriyat Conference, was shot dead by gunmen in police uniform at a rally at the Idgah in Srinagar on 21 May 2002. The rally marked the anniversary of Mirwaiz Mohammad Farooq's killing, and the attack came a day before Prime Minister Vajpayee's visit to the Valley.

title: Qasim Nagar massacre
summary: On the night of 13 July 2002 militants fired on a settlement of poor labourers living in makeshift shelters at Qasim Nagar on the edge of Jammu city. Between 24 and 29 people were killed according to different accounts.

title: Attack on Amarnath pilgrims at Nunwan base camp
summary: At dawn on 6 August 2002 a militant dressed as a local herder got through the security cordon at the Nunwan base camp, threw grenades and fired at pilgrims. Nine pilgrims were killed and 28 injured before he was shot dead. Deputy Prime Minister L.K. Advani blamed al-Mansuriyan, a new front of Lashkar-e-Taiba.

title: Second fidayeen attack on Raghunath temple, Jammu
place_name: Raghunath temple and nearby Shiv temple, Jammu city
summary: On 24 November 2002, eight months after the first attack, Lashkar-e-Taiba fidayeen stormed the Raghunath temple when it was crowded with devotees and also attacked a nearby Shiv temple. At least 12 people were killed, including four women and two security men, and about 50 were injured.

title: Nadimarg massacre
summary: On the night of 22 to 23 March 2003 Lashkar-e-Taiba militants in combat uniforms surrounded the Kashmiri Pandit homes in Nadimarg, lined up the residents and shot them. Twenty-four people were killed: 11 men, 11 women and two small boys. The High Court later ordered the stalled trial to resume.

title: Fidayeen attack on Sunjwan army camp, Jammu
summary: On 28 June 2003 two fidayeen cut through the wire at the Sunjwan army camp in Jammu and attacked soldiers in their barracks. Twelve soldiers, including an officer, were killed and seven wounded before both attackers died.

title: Fidayeen attack on army camp at Tanda, Akhnoor
summary: On 22 July 2003 fidayeen stormed an army camp at Akhnoor near Jammu. Eight soldiers including a brigadier were killed, and 12 were injured, among them senior generals visiting the camp.

title: India and Pakistan agree to a ceasefire on the LoC
place_name: Line of Control, International Border and Siachen
summary: India and Pakistan agreed on 26 November 2003 to a ceasefire along the Line of Control, the International Border and Siachen. Firing largely stopped for several years, before violations rose again from 2008 and peaked in 2020.

title: Fidayeen attack on Tourist Reception Centre before the Srinagar to Muzaffarabad bus
summary: On 6 April 2005, hours before the first bus between Srinagar and Muzaffarabad was due to leave, two militants attacked the Tourist Reception Centre in Srinagar where passengers were staying. All passengers were evacuated, both attackers were killed, and six people including a constable were injured.

title: Killing of minister Dr Ghulam Nabi Lone
summary: Dr Ghulam Nabi Lone, a minister in the state government who had been education minister, was killed in a militant attack at Tulsibagh, Srinagar on 18 October 2005. He was one of several mainstream politicians targeted in the Valley in the 2000s.

title: Suicide car bomb at Nowgam, Srinagar
summary: On 2 November 2005 a suicide bomber set off a car bomb at Nowgam on the outskirts of Srinagar. Ten people were killed, including a 10-year-old boy, a woman passer-by, three police personnel and the bomber, and about 15 were wounded. Jaish-e-Mohammed claimed the attack.

title: Killing of Hindu shepherds at Lalon Galla, Basantgarh
place_name: Lalon Galla meadow above Basantgarh, Udhampur
summary: On the same night as the Doda killings, another militant unit forced two local Muslim herders to guide them to a high meadow above Basantgarh, where Hindu herdsmen had set up their summer camp. Thirteen shepherds were shot dead.

title: Kulhand and Tharwa massacre, Doda
summary: Late on 30 April 2006 a group of six militants entered the hamlets of Kulhand and Tharwa in Doda, gathered the Hindu men at the village headman's house, lined them up and shot them. Nineteen people, including an eight-year-old girl, were killed according to one detailed account. Lashkar-e-Taiba was held responsible.

title: IED attack on army convoy at Narbal
summary: On 19 July 2008 militants set off an IED under an army bus in a convoy at Narbal on the Srinagar to Baramulla highway. Ten soldiers were killed and about 20 injured.

title: Fidayeen hostage attack at Chinore, Jammu
summary: On 27 August 2008 three fidayeen who had crossed from the Kanachak sector hijacked a load carrier, drove about 15 km and stormed a house at Chinore near Jammu, taking a family hostage. Eleven people were killed, including three soldiers, five civilians and the three attackers.

title: Fidayeen attack on CRPF at Bemina, Srinagar
summary: On the morning of 13 March 2013 two militants threw grenades and opened fire on a CRPF party at Bemina in Srinagar. Five CRPF personnel and both attackers were killed.

title: Ambush on army convoy at Hyderpora, Srinagar
summary: On 24 June 2013, a day before a visit by Prime Minister Manmohan Singh, militants ambushed an army bus at Hyderpora on the outskirts of Srinagar. Eight soldiers were killed and 16 injured. Hizbul Mujahideen claimed the attack, but police found Lashkar-e-Taiba was behind it.

title: Twin fidayeen attacks at Hiranagar police station and Samba army camp
summary: On 26 September 2013 three militants who had crossed from Pakistan attacked the Hiranagar police station in Kathua, killing four policemen, then struck an army camp in Samba where four soldiers including Lt Col Bikramjeet Singh were killed. At least ten people died in total, and all three attackers were killed.

title: Fidayeen attack on army camp at Mohura, Uri
summary: On 5 December 2014 heavily armed fidayeen stormed an army ordnance camp at Mohura in the Uri sector near the Line of Control. Eleven security personnel were killed: a lieutenant colonel and seven soldiers, and three Jammu and Kashmir policemen.

title: Fidayeen attack on Rajbagh police station, Kathua
place_name: Rajbagh police station, Jammu to Pathankot highway, Kathua
summary: On 20 March 2015 two attackers in combat dress stormed the Rajbagh police station on the Jammu to Pathankot highway in Kathua, about 15 km from the International Border. Three security personnel, two of them from the CRPF, and two civilians were killed, and both attackers, believed to be from Lashkar-e-Taiba, were shot dead after a gunfight of several hours.

title: Attack on BSF convoy at Udhampur and capture of Mohammed Naved
place_name: Simroli, Jammu to Srinagar highway, Udhampur
summary: On the morning of 5 August 2015 two Lashkar-e-Taiba militants fired on a BSF convoy on the national highway at Simroli near Udhampur, killing two constables. One attacker was shot dead. The other, Mohammed Naved of Faisalabad in Pakistan, fled and took villagers hostage, but the villagers overpowered him and handed him to police.

title: Attack on CRPF bus at Pampore
place_name: Frestbal, Pampore, Srinagar to Jammu highway
summary: On 25 June 2016 militants fired on a CRPF bus on the national highway at Frestbal near Pampore. Eight CRPF personnel were killed and about 20 injured, and two attackers were killed.

title: Hizbul commander Burhan Wani killed at Bamdoora, Kokernag
summary: Hizbul Mujahideen commander Burhan Wani, who had drawn young recruits through social media, was killed in an encounter with security forces at Bamdoora near Kokernag on 8 July 2016. His death set off months of unrest across the Valley.

title: Fidayeen attack on Uri brigade headquarters
summary: Before dawn on 18 September 2016 four fidayeen attacked the army's brigade headquarters at Uri. Seventeen soldiers were killed in the first count, in what was reported as the deadliest attack on the brigade, and all four attackers died. India answered with cross-LoC strikes eleven days later.

title: Surgical strikes on terrorist launch pads across the LoC
place_name: Launch pads across the Line of Control
summary: On the night of 28 to 29 September 2016 Indian special forces crossed the Line of Control and struck terrorist launch pads where teams were waiting to infiltrate. The then DGMO, Lt Gen Ranbir Singh, announced the strikes the next morning. The army later said it had no record of earlier operations of this kind.

title: Fidayeen attack on Nagrota army base
place_name: Army camp at Nagrota, near Jammu
summary: Early on 29 November 2016 three fidayeen stormed an army base at Nagrota near Jammu. Seven soldiers, including two majors, and the three attackers were killed. The case was later linked in court to a Jaish-e-Mohammed module.

title: Attack on Amarnath pilgrims' bus at Batengoo
summary: On the evening of 10 July 2017 Lashkar-e-Taiba militants fired on a bus carrying Amarnath pilgrims, most from Gujarat, at Batengoo near Khanabal. The bus was travelling outside the protected convoy. Eight pilgrims were killed. Police later charged Lashkar-e-Taiba and 11 people.

title: Fidayeen attack on Sunjuwan military station
summary: Before dawn on 10 February 2018 three Jaish-e-Mohammed fidayeen entered the family quarters of the Sunjuwan military station in Jammu. Six soldiers and a civilian were killed and about 20 people injured, including women and children, before all three attackers were killed.

title: Abduction and killing of Rifleman Aurangzeb
summary: Rifleman Aurangzeb of 44 Rashtriya Rifles was abducted by militants on 14 June 2018 while going home for Eid, and his body was found hours later at Gussu village in Pulwama. He was awarded the Shaurya Chakra, and his brothers later joined the Army.

title: Killing of editor Shujaat Bukhari and his guards
summary: Shujaat Bukhari, editor-in-chief of Rising Kashmir, was shot dead outside his office in Press Enclave, Srinagar on the evening of 14 June 2018, along with his two police guards. Police linked the killing to Lashkar-e-Taiba, and a Pakistan-based plotter was later designated a terrorist.

title: Pulwama suicide car bombing of CRPF convoy
place_name: Lethpora, Pulwama, Jammu to Srinagar highway
summary: On 14 February 2019 a Jaish-e-Mohammed suicide bomber, Adil Ahmad Dar, drove a vehicle packed with explosives into a bus in a CRPF convoy of about 70 vehicles at Lethpora on the Jammu to Srinagar highway. Forty CRPF personnel were killed, among the deadliest attacks on Indian security forces in Kashmir. India responded with an air strike on a Jaish camp at Balakot twelve days later.

title: Air strike on Jaish-e-Mohammed camp at Balakot
summary: Before dawn on 26 February 2019 Indian Air Force jets struck what the government called the biggest Jaish-e-Mohammed training camp, at Balakot in Pakistan. The Foreign Secretary described it as a non-military, pre-emptive strike based on intelligence that more suicide attacks were being planned. No official casualty figure was released.

title: Pakistani air raid and capture of Wing Commander Abhinandan Varthaman
place_name: Nowshera and Rajouri sectors, and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir
summary: A day after Balakot, Pakistani jets tried to strike military targets across the Line of Control. In the air battle that followed, Wing Commander Abhinandan Varthaman's MiG-21 was shot down and he ejected over Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, where he was captured. He was handed back on 1 March 2019 and later awarded the Vir Chakra for shooting down a Pakistani jet.

title: Jamaat-e-Islami Jammu and Kashmir declared an unlawful association
summary: On 28 February 2019, after the Pulwama attack, the Home Ministry declared Jamaat-e-Islami Jammu and Kashmir an unlawful association under the UAPA. The ban was extended for a further five years in 2024.

title: JKLF declared an unlawful association
summary: On 22 March 2019 the Home Ministry banned Yasin Malik's JKLF under the UAPA, accusing it of funding terrorism and of responsibility for killings of Kashmiri Pandits in 1989 that led to their exodus. A UAPA tribunal later upheld extensions of the ban.

title: Article 370 provisions revoked and the state reorganised
summary: On 5 August 2019 Parliament ended the special status of Jammu and Kashmir under Article 370 and passed the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, which split the state into two Union Territories. The Supreme Court upheld the decision on 11 December 2023.

title: Killing of five labourers from West Bengal at Katrasoo, Kulgam
summary: On 29 October 2019 militants shot dead five labourers from Murshidabad in West Bengal at Katrasoo village in Kulgam, where they had worked in orchards for years, and injured a sixth. The victims' bodies were flown home to Murshidabad.

title: Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh come into being
summary: The Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh came into existence on 31 October 2019. The new official maps of 2 November 2019 placed Pakistan-occupied Mirpur, Muzaffarabad and Poonch in the UT of Jammu and Kashmir, and Gilgit-Baltistan in the UT of Ladakh.

title: Handwara encounter, Colonel and Major among five killed
summary: On 2 May 2020 a Rashtriya Rifles team led by Colonel Ashutosh Sharma entered a house in Handwara where militants were holding civilians. The civilians were rescued, but five security personnel, including the Colonel, Major Anuj Sood and a police sub-inspector, were killed along with two militants.

title: Hizbul Mujahideen chief Riyaz Naikoo killed at Beighpora
summary: Riyaz Naikoo, operations chief of Hizbul Mujahideen in Kashmir and successor to Burhan Wani, was killed with an associate in an encounter in his home village of Beighpora on 6 May 2020. He had been the most wanted militant in the Valley.

title: Killing of sarpanch Ajay Pandita
summary: Ajay Pandita, a Kashmiri Pandit and elected sarpanch of Lokbawan Larkipora in Anantnag, was shot dead by militants on 8 June 2020. His killing raised fears among the few Pandits who had stayed in or returned to the Valley and among elected village representatives.

title: Galwan valley clash with China
summary: On the night of 15 to 16 June 2020 Indian and Chinese troops clashed in the Galwan valley along the Line of Actual Control. No shots were fired, but Chinese troops used clubs studded with nails. Twenty Indian soldiers were killed, including the commanding officer of 16 Bihar, Colonel B. Santosh Babu, who was awarded the Maha Vir Chakra.

title: Drone attack on the Air Force station at Jammu
summary: In the early hours of 27 June 2021 two explosive devices dropped by drones exploded at the Air Force station in Jammu, five minutes apart. Two airmen were slightly injured and a building was damaged. It was the first drone attack on an Indian military installation, and investigators said the explosives pointed to Pakistani ordnance factories.

title: Killing of chemist Makhan Lal Bindroo
summary: Makhan Lal Bindroo, 68, a Kashmiri Pandit who owned one of Srinagar's best-known pharmacies, was shot dead at his shop on 5 October 2021. Two other civilians were killed within hours the same evening. Police blamed The Resistance Front.

title: Killing of street vendor Virender Paswan
summary: Virender Paswan, a street food vendor from Bhagalpur in Bihar and the sole earner for his family, was shot dead in Srinagar on the evening of 5 October 2021, hours after Makhan Lal Bindroo. He was cremated in Srinagar without his family present.

title: Killing of principal Supinder Kaur and teacher Deepak Chand
summary: On 7 October 2021 gunmen entered a government school at Eidgah in Srinagar, checked the staff's identities, let the Muslim teachers go and shot dead the Sikh principal Supinder Kaur and the Hindu teacher Deepak Chand. The Resistance Front claimed the killing.

title: Ambush on army search party in Surankote forests
summary: On 11 October 2021 militants hiding in the forests of Surankote in Poonch fired on an army search party, killing a junior commissioned officer and four soldiers. The operation spread to Mendhar and Thanamandi and became one of the longest in the Pir Panjal belt.

title: Soldiers killed in Bhata Durian forests, Mendhar
summary: Three days after the Surankote ambush, troops combing the Bhata Durian forests in Mendhar were fired on from a hillock on 14 October 2021. Two soldiers including a junior commissioned officer were killed that evening, and the bodies of two more were recovered later, taking the army's toll for the week to nine.

title: Killing of two labourers from Bihar at Wanpoh, Kulgam
summary: On the evening of 17 October 2021 militants burst into a rented room at Wanpoh in Kulgam and shot dead two labourers from Bihar, injuring a third. The killings, part of a wave of attacks on outside workers that month, led many migrant labourers to leave the Valley.

title: Killing of revenue employee Rahul Bhat
summary: Rahul Bhat, a Kashmiri Pandit clerk working in the Chadoora tehsil office, was shot inside his office on 12 May 2022 and died in hospital. He lived in a transit colony for Pandit employees at Sheikhpora. His killing set off months of protests by Pandit employees demanding transfer out of the Valley.

title: Killing of teacher Rajni Bala
summary: Rajni Bala, a Hindu teacher from Samba in the Jammu region, was shot dead at the gate of the government high school at Gopalpora in Kulgam on 31 May 2022, shortly after her husband dropped her at work. Students and staff later held a memorial for her at the school.

title: Killing of Bihar labourer Dilkhush Kumar at a Chadoora brick kiln
summary: On the night of 2 June 2022, hours after the killing of bank manager Vijay Kumar, militants fired on two brick kiln workers at Magraypora in Chadoora. Dilkhush Kumar, 17, from Bihar, died, and a co-worker from Punjab was injured.

title: Killing of bank manager Vijay Kumar
place_name: Ellaquai Dehati Bank, Arreh Mohanpora, Kulgam
summary: Vijay Kumar, a 29-year-old bank manager from Rajasthan, was shot inside his branch of the Ellaquai Dehati Bank at Arreh Mohanpora in Kulgam on 2 June 2022 and died on the way to hospital. It was the eighth targeted killing in the Valley since 1 May that year.

title: Killing of Sunil Kumar Bhat in his orchard
summary: Militants shot dead Sunil Kumar Bhat, a Kashmiri Pandit who had never left the Valley, and injured his relative in their apple orchard at Chotigam in Shopian on 16 August 2022. His relative survived with injuries.

title: Killing of Puran Krishan Bhat
summary: Puran Krishan Bhat was shot dead outside his ancestral home at Chowdhary Gund in Shopian on 15 October 2022, where he had gone to look after his orchard. Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha visited the family and promised a job and other help.

title: Dhangri massacre, Rajouri
summary: On the evening of 1 January 2023 two terrorists went from house to house in Dhangri village, checking identities and shooting Hindu residents, killing five. The next morning an explosive device they had left behind went off and killed two children. The NIA named Pakistan-based Lashkar handlers as the planners.

title: Killing of bank guard Sanjay Sharma
summary: Sanjay Sharma, a 40-year-old Kashmiri Pandit who worked as a bank guard, was shot at close range on a street leading to his house in the village of Achan in Pulwama on the morning of 26 February 2023. His Muslim neighbours mourned him, and the militant accused was later killed by security forces.

title: Ambush on army truck at Bhata Dhurian, Poonch
place_name: Bhata Dhurian, Bhimber Gali to Sanjiote road, Poonch
summary: On 20 April 2023 militants ambushed an army truck moving from Bhimber Gali to Sanjiote at Bhata Dhurian in Poonch, firing assault rifles and throwing grenades. The truck caught fire and five soldiers were killed. Investigators said the attackers had studied the target and used armour-piercing rounds.

title: IED blast kills five para commandos in Kandi forests, Rajouri
summary: On 5 May 2023 militants cornered in the Kesari hills near Kandi set off a remote-controlled explosive as special forces closed in. Five para commandos were killed and a major was injured. The attack followed the pattern of militants drawing troops into prepared positions in the forests.

title: Gadole encounter in Kokernag forests
summary: On 13 September 2023 a search party moving up towards a militant hideout at Gadole in the Kokernag forests came under fire. Colonel Manpreet Singh, Major Ashish Dhonchak and Deputy Superintendent Humayun Bhat were among those killed. The operation lasted a week and ended with two militants, including commander Uzair Khan, killed. Four or five security personnel died in all, depending on the account.

title: Kalakote encounter, two captains among soldiers killed
summary: On 22 November 2023 an army search team in the Baaji Maal area of Kalakote came under fire from militants. Two captains and two soldiers were killed in the first day of fighting.

title: Ambush on army vehicles near Dera Ki Gali, Poonch
place_name: Dhatyar Morh, between Dera Ki Gali and Bafliaz, Poonch
summary: On the afternoon of 21 December 2023 militants fired on two army vehicles carrying troops on the Surankote to Thanamandi road near Dera Ki Gali. Four soldiers were killed and three injured.

title: Attack on pilgrims' bus at Reasi
place_name: Near Teryath, Ransoo area, Reasi (Shiv Khori to Katra road)
victim_community: Hindu pilgrims from Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Delhi
summary: On the evening of 9 June 2024 militants fired on a bus taking pilgrims from the Shiv Khori shrine to Katra, and the bus fell into a gorge. Nine people were killed, including three women and two children, and dozens were injured. The NIA later charged accused linked to Lashkar-e-Taiba.

title: Militant attack at Saida Sukhal, Hiranagar
summary: Two days after Reasi, two militants who had crossed the border fired on villagers in Saida Sukhal near Hiranagar on the evening of 11 June 2024. Both were killed by the next day, and CRPF constable Kabir Das died of his wounds.

title: Ambush on army patrol at Badnota, Machedi, Kathua
place_name: Badnota, Machedi to Kindli road, Kathua
summary: On the afternoon of 8 July 2024 militants hit an army truck with a grenade and gunfire on a remote road near Badnota in Kathua. Five soldiers, including a junior commissioned officer, were killed and five injured. A Jaish-e-Mohammed front, Kashmir Tigers, claimed the attack.

title: Desa forest encounter, Doda
summary: On the night of 15 July 2024 troops chasing militants in the Desa forest of Doda came under heavy fire. Captain Brijesh Thapa and three soldiers were killed, and the militants escaped deeper into the forest.

title: Attack on Z-Morh tunnel workers' camp, Gagangir
victim_community: Construction workers and a local doctor
summary: On the evening of 20 October 2024 militants fired on the camp of workers building the Z-Morh tunnel at Gagangir, on the road to Sonamarg. Six workers and a local doctor were killed and five injured. A Lashkar-e-Taiba militant involved was later killed.

title: Attack on army vehicle at Botapathri near Gulmarg
summary: On the evening of 24 October 2024 militants fired on a Rashtriya Rifles vehicle at Botapathri, a few kilometres from the Gulmarg ski resort. Two soldiers and two civilian porters working with the army were killed.

title: Pahalgam massacre at Baisaran meadow
victim_community: Tourists, targeted after being asked their religion
summary: On the afternoon of 22 April 2025 militants opened fire on visitors at the Baisaran meadow above Pahalgam, after asking about their religious identity. Twenty-six people were killed, most of them tourists. The Resistance Front first claimed the attack and then withdrew the claim. The NIA charged Lashkar-e-Taiba, the TRF and Pakistan-based handlers.

title: Operation Sindoor strikes on terror camps in Pakistan and PoJK
place_name: Bahawalpur, Muridke, Sialkot, Tehra Kalan and Barnala in Pakistan; Muzaffarabad and Kotli in PoJK
summary: In the early hours of 7 May 2025 India struck nine sites in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir linked to Jaish-e-Mohammed, Lashkar-e-Taiba and Hizbul Mujahideen, including Jaish-e-Mohammed's Markaz Subhan Allah at Bahawalpur and Lashkar-e-Taiba's Markaz Taiba at Muridke. The government said no Pakistani military facilities were targeted in this first wave. Four days of fighting followed before a ceasefire understanding on 10 May.

title: Pakistani shelling of Poonch and Tangdhar
place_name: Poonch town and villages along the LoC, and Tangdhar
victim_community: Residents of Poonch including Sikh worshippers
summary: Within an hour of Operation Sindoor on 7 May 2025, Pakistan's army shelled towns and villages along the Line of Control. Poonch town was hit hardest, including a gurdwara, and at least a dozen civilians were killed and dozens injured on the first day alone.

title: India and Pakistan agree to stop firing
place_name: Line of Control and International Border
summary: On the afternoon of 10 May 2025 Pakistan's DGMO called his Indian counterpart, and both sides agreed to stop all firing on land, in the air and at sea from 5 pm. India accused Pakistan of violating the understanding the same night.

title: Pakistani shell kills Rajouri official Raj Kumar Thapa
summary: In the early hours of 10 May 2025 a Pakistani artillery shell hit the official residence of Raj Kumar Thapa, Additional District Development Commissioner of Rajouri, killing him and wounding two staff members. Two other civilians were killed in Rajouri that morning.

title: Operation Mahadev kills the Pahalgam attackers near Dachigam
summary: After a hunt of about three months, security forces killed three Pakistani terrorists in the Dachigam and Harwan forests near Srinagar on 28 July 2025. The Home Minister told Parliament they were Suleman Shah, Jibran and Hamza Afghani, the men behind the Pahalgam massacre.

title: Special forces soldier killed in Kishtwar encounter
summary: Havildar Gajendra Singh of the Special Forces was killed on 19 January 2026 during an operation in the Singpura area of Kishtwar, in which hiding militants threw grenades. Eight soldiers were injured, mostly by splinters.

title: Three Jaish-e-Mohammed militants killed in Udhampur and Kishtwar
summary: Security forces killed three Jaish-e-Mohammed militants, said to include commanders, in separate encounters in Udhampur and Kishtwar districts in early February 2026. Two of them were named in reports as Jaish commanders.

title: Labourer from Chhattisgarh killed at a Kulgam brick kiln
summary: On 31 July 2026 militants fired on two labourers from Chhattisgarh at a brick kiln in the Kelam area of Kulgam. One died before he could reach hospital and the other was injured.

title: Lashkar commander Moosa killed at Korag, Yusmarg
summary: In late September 2026 security forces killed Mohammad Asif, known as Moosa or Asif Fauji, in the higher reaches of Korag near Yusmarg. Officials described him as a former soldier of the Pakistan Army's Special Services Group who led Lashkar operations in the region, and the Home Ministry called his killing a serious blow to the group.

title: Lashkar militant Yasir killed in Yusmarg heights
summary: Security forces killed a Lashkar-e-Taiba militant identified by police as Yasir in the Yusmarg heights of Budgam on 5 September 2026. He was a close associate of the commander known as Moosa.
